chunks: I said to him: It has reached me that you say that whoever divorces contrary to the Sunnah, you do not consider his divorce as anything.

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I am not saying it — rather it is God, Mighty and Majestic, Who says it. By God! If we were to issue fatwas to you with injustice, we would be worse than you, because God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'Why do not the Rabbis and the scholars prohibit them from their speaking of what is sinful and their eating of what is unlawfully acquired?'
— up to the end of the verse.

key_terms.الرَّبَّانِيُّون: Rabbaniyun — scholars deeply grounded in divine knowledge and God-consciousness
key_terms.السُّحْت: Suht — unlawfully acquired wealth, often used for bribes or earnings from forbidden sources
key_terms.الْأَحْبَار: Ahbar — Jewish or Christian scholars/monks; here invoked as a type of religious authority
key_terms.الْجَوْر: Injustice, inequity — issuing rulings that deviate from divine law
key_terms.لِغَيْرِ السُّنَّةِ: Contrary to the Sunnah — refers to a divorce that does not follow the prescribed Islamic procedure (e.g., during menses, or without witnesses, or by triple pronouncement)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about divorce contrary to the Sunnah and the responsibility of religious scholars?
ai.summary: Abu Basir reports that he questioned Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the ruling that divorce contrary to the Sunnah is invalid. The Imam corrected the framing by asserting that this ruling comes not from him but from God Almighty, citing Quran 5:63. He then issued a stern warning: if the Imams were to sanction injustice, they would be more blameworthy than anyone, for God has condemned religious authorities who permit sin and unlawful gain.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, from Amro Bin Riyah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It has reached me that you<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who divorces to other than the Sunnah, you<sup>asws</sup> do not view his divorce as anything?’

So Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Iasws am not saying it, but Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying it. By Allahazwj! If weasws were to issue a Verdict/Fatwas with the inequity weasws would be more evil than you all because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying
[5:63] Why do not the Rabbis and the Monks prohibit them from their speaking of what is sinful and their eating of what is unlawfully acquired?
– up to the end of the Verse’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Aban from abu Basir from “Amr ibn Riyah who has said the following: “I once said to abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Have you said that one who does not divorce according to the book and al -Sunnah his divorce is not valid?’

Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, replied, ‘I have not said so, in fact, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said it. By Allah, were we to give you fatwas with injustice we would become worse than you; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘
Would that their Rabbis and Ahbar prohibit them from their sinful words and consuming what is filthy. . . .’
